title: Collatz Conjecture: Reduction to Odd Inputs

problemStatement.formal: \text{Let } \mathrm{ReachesOne}(n) \equiv \exists k,\ T^k(n)=1 \text{ where } T(n)=n/2\ (2\mid n),\ 3n+1\ (\text{else}). \text{ Show } (\forall n\ge1,\ \mathrm{ReachesOne}\,n) \iff (\forall \text{ odd } m\ge1,\ \mathrm{ReachesOne}\,m).
problemStatement.plain: The Collatz conjecture asks whether every positive integer reaches 1 under n→n/2 (even), n→3n+1 (odd). This entry proves, axiom-free, that the conjecture is equivalent to its restriction to odd inputs — reducing the search space. The conjecture itself stays open.
whyMatters: Standard first simplification of the Collatz problem, now formalized
Establishes the reaching set as invariant under the dynamics and under powers of two

proven: Powers of 2 reach 1; reaching set closed under doubling (parent collatz-structured)
One-step invariance: ReachesOne (collatz n) ↔ ReachesOne n (this entry, 0 axioms)
Power-of-two invariance: ReachesOne (2^m·n) ↔ ReachesOne n (this entry, 0 axioms)
Reduction to odd: (∀ n≥1, ReachesOne n) ↔ (∀ odd m≥1, ReachesOne m) (this entry, 0 axioms)
open: The Collatz conjecture itself (every odd n ≥ 1 reaches 1)
Further reduction (n ≡ 3 mod 4, or the Syracuse accelerated odd map)
knownResults.goal: Formalize structural reductions of the Collatz conjecture; the full conjecture is open.

knowledge.progressSummary: FORMALIZED (0 axioms): reduced the Collatz conjecture to odd inputs via one-step and power-of-two invariance of the reaching set. The conjecture itself remains open.
builtItems: collatz_counterexample_odd — counterexamples may be taken odd
insights: The reaching set is invariant under the Collatz map in BOTH directions; the only non-formal point is the n=1 forward base case (collatz 1 = 4 = 2²).
Doubling closure (parent) upgrades to an equivalence using forward one-step invariance + collatz(2n)=n.
Mathlib's ordProj/ordCompl factorization (n = 2^v₂(n)·oddPart n) makes the odd reduction a few lines.
The file imports the parent (which axiomatizes the conjecture) but uses no axiom — genuinely verified.
